name: Hacker News
measures: Stance in sampled comments, job posts and topic mentions
about: Every month the Hacker News whoishiring account opens a thread where companies post jobs, and we count the top-level comments. We also count how many comments mention a fixed list of phrases each month. A sample of comments is labeled for stance by an AI model, Claude Haiku. We publish only totals, never comment text or usernames.
attribution: Counts derived from the Hacker News API and the Algolia HN Search API, Y Combinator. Comments belong to their authors and are not stored.
limitations: It reflects a startup-heavy, English-speaking audience.
Top-level comments are mostly job posts, but not all, and a post can list several roles.
Deleted comments can still be counted.
A phrase match is not an opinion: a comment can mention a phrase to disagree with it.
In a sample check, about 85% of "vibe coding" matches contained the exact phrase, so search counts are approximate.

Stance labels come from an AI model and make mistakes, especially with sarcasm. Every "getting solved" label was checked by a second AI reviewer and 11 of 39 were corrected. The much larger "not solved" group was not fully checked, so it likely contains errors.
The sample covers up to 50 comments per month that mention specific phrases, so it does not represent all of Hacker News.
